audit.why: 48.8% over 2877 games and a 6/10 EVEN rating are the right shape for a lane Riven wins for three levels and then loses to armour. Levels 1-3 are hers because her combo exists and his does not; from the first armour item the trade maths invert permanently.
audit.corrected: No change to diff, diffRating or carryRating. The chart is where this matchup was wrong, not the summary.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagreed with the packet, and three of them disagreed with the prose printed directly beneath them. The page gave Riven First item and 2+ items while whys[5] says 'sustained trades now favour him' and whys[6] says 'your role is Wind Slash cleanup, not the primary carry threat'. Level 6 said Skill while whys[4] says 'he controls this window'. Level 1 said Skill against a packet reading of Riven.
audit.why: The mirror agent found the same four fields on the opposite page and could not fix them — their note says swapping 'Riven' (5 chars) to 'Malphite' (8 chars) is +60% and they assumed the applier would reject it. That assumption is wrong: phases[N].side and win[N] are ENUM_FIELD and are exempt from the length band, and the applier also skips any string under 25 characters. So the flip applies cleanly and this is exactly the case the run has been losing champions to.
audit.corrected: Proposed as one atomic chart group in matched full/content pairs: row 0 -> Riven, rows 4, 5 and 6 -> Malphite, with ratings 7/10, 4/10, 3/10, 2/10. Row 3 (Levels 4-5, Skill) already agreed. Every row now matches both the packet and the why beneath it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield is described as armour in spikes[0].text ('his passive armor absorbs a full rotation') and vaguely as a 'bubble' elsewhere. It is a shield worth up to 10% of his maximum health that recharges when he has not been hit for a few seconds. And Ground Slam — the ability that actually decides the mid-lane — is never named or numbered anywhere on the page.
audit.why: The Ground Slam interaction is the best fact available in this matchup and it was missing entirely. Riven's passive charges her blade with abilities but only her basic attacks cash the charges, so Ground Slam's attack-speed reduction does not merely lower her DPS on paper — it strands Runic Blade charges she has already paid for. It is a flat 7s cooldown at 400 range, which means in any extended trade it is up again before her combo is. Separately, calling the passive 'armor' tells the player to look for armour penetration when the answer is simply to break the shield with any damage and keep hitting him so it never recharges.
audit.corrected: Granite Shield's 10%-max-health shield and its recharge-on-no-damage condition written into whys[0], spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0] and report[5].t. Ground Slam named with its 7s cooldown and the Runic Blade consequence in whys[3], wants.foe[1] and report[5].t. Unstoppable Force's 1000 range and 130s rank-1 cooldown into dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The displacement race never reaches the page.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags knockup-enabler: Broken Wings' third cast knocks back and Unstoppable Force knocks up, and whoever lands theirs first owns the trade because the loser is displaced out of their own follow-up. The page tells the player to bait his R but never tells her that landing Q3 first is itself the answer.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] rewritten around winning the displacement race.

unverified: The kit file puts a grounding flag on both Seismic Shard (Q) and Ground Slam (E). Riot's text for neither mentions grounding — Q steals move speed, E reduces attack speed. If either genuinely grounded, it would be the single most important fact in this matchup for a champion with three dashes, so it is worth a human confirming rather than me asserting it from a flag that contradicts the description. Nothing I wrote depends on it either way.
The claim in late that his R is 'a 1.5-second hard interrupt'. Riot's text gives no knockup duration. Left the sentence alone rather than change a number I cannot check.

The onhit-itemization interaction on Thunderclap (W) — the flag says it applies on-hit and scales with attack speed. The page's existing 'W-empowered auto' references are consistent with that, so I added nothing new, but no field currently tells the player attack speed is what scales it.
notes: The important finding here is procedural, not mechanical: the mirror agent skipped four correct chart edits because they believed a 5-char to 8-char enum swap would be rejected for length. It would not be. If other agents on this run made the same assumption, malphite's opposite page (malphite__riven, phases[5]/[6] and win[5]/[6]) is still showing Riven as the winner of both late stages against a 54.68% Malphite win rate, and should be re-run.
